title: Sharp Second-Order Constant for a Three-Arm Contrast against Two Averaged Comparators
banked_reason: D0.5.G: tier=subfield below floor=field and not salvageable in scope; final dependency-closure audit PASS, with the raw math objection adjudicated as notation ambiguity rather than a mathematical defect.
gap_reasons: The note proves matched global second-order minimax expansions through a schedule-uniform estimator and an all-design Bayes lower bound, but it does not prove the stronger fiberwise liminf/recovery comparison posed in oeq:uniform-singular-bridge; the framing accurately leaves that comparison open.

The contribution is confined to one labelled three-arm contrast and common bounded outcome intervals, with no general multi-arm characterization or substantive application demonstrating the practical magnitude of the second-order gain.

The package remains confined to one fixed three-arm contrast and does not present the advertised exact n=3 label-gap computation or numerical finite-sample certificates, limiting its significance for a leading econometrics journal.
proof_attempt_summary: The run derived and repeatedly audited a common global second-order Airy constant, matching schedule-uniform and all-design Bayes bounds, exact bounded-endpoint transfer, and the local iid allocation frontier. It repaired the Airy remainder, Van Trees dependency, allocation subsequence case, and assignment-conditioned orbit symmetrization, leaving the resulting global value package mathematically sound. The promised uniform fiberwise face/corner experiment bridge remains open, so the fixed-contrast result did not clear the field novelty floor and was banked at subfield.
tldr: For the fixed three-arm contrast \(1,-1/2,-1/2\) and any common finite outcome interval \[L,U\], an exact endpoint-transfer theorem makes the unrestricted and iid bounded minimax values \(U-L\)^2 times their binary values. The eight-type orbit game remains a literal reduction only for binary endpoint schedules. The new proved kernel identifies the half-wedge Airy constant \(C_3=-a_1^{\prime}\), establishes matching global minimax-value bounds through schedule-uniform estimators and all-design priors, and gives the sharp \(n^{-1/6}\) iid allocation frontier. A stronger fiberwise uniform liminf/recovery comparison across transverse strata remains open.
gap: The accepted repository parent settles the lossless exact multi-arm orbit reduction, but it does not identify the second-order constant, control the singular transverse fiber, or characterize allocation perturbations at the scale where first-order design loss meets nonlinear minimax gain.
fill: The project derives the exact half-wedge Airy constant, proves a uniform finite-orbit bridge with null-cell and dormant-constraint control, constructs matching upper and lower procedures, and establishes the necessary-and-sufficient \(n^{-1/6}\) allocation frontier.
